title: MIT NANDA report finds 95% of enterprise generative AI pilots show little or no P&L impact
summary: Fortune reports that MIT's NANDA initiative, in its report 'The GenAI Divide: State of AI in Business 2025', drew on 150 interviews with leaders, a survey of 350 employees and an analysis of 300 public AI deployments, and found that only about 5% of enterprise AI pilots achieve rapid revenue acceleration while the rest stall with little to no measurable P&L impact. The report attributes this to a learning gap in tools and organisations rather than to model quality, finds that purchasing from specialised vendors and building partnerships succeeds about 67% of the time while internal builds succeed about one-third as often, and mentions agentic systems only as a next phase that the most advanced organisations are experimenting with.
verification_note: URL fetched 2026-10-17; Fortune page dated August 18, 2025 (author Sheryl Estrada), not paywalled. Figures (150 interviews, 350-employee survey, 300 deployments, 5% vs 95%, 67% vendor-partnership success, internal builds one-third as often) confirmed from the article body. Marked not relevant: the report covers enterprise generative AI pilots in general (generic tools such as ChatGPT); agents that take actions appear only as a forward-looking aside, not as the subject of the findings.
